title: Chinese Communists
capsule: Within the 1928–1932 window the Chinese Communist Party existed as an armed insurgent movement carving out rural base areas after the Kuomintang's 1927 purge had driven it from the cities. Mao Zedong and Zhu De established the Jinggangshan base on the Jiangxi–Hunan border in 1928, and in November 1931 the scattered soviets coalesced into the Chinese Soviet Republic, proclaimed at Ruijin in Jiangxi with Mao as chairman. This territorial soviet — the entity the dataset attests at roughly 27°N 114°E — survived successive Nationalist 'encirclement campaigns' until pressure forced the Communists to abandon it in the Long March of 1934.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The CCP's controlled territory during 1932–1949 is incompletely mapped; borders of the Jiangxi Soviet and Yan'an base area are approximated from historical accounts rather than administrative surveys, and front lines shifted rapidly throughout the Civil War period.
